verdict.rationale: Rive's own docs say editor output is what ships: an exported .riv file plays across web, mobile, and game-engine runtimes via open-source runtime libraries, and data binding links the design to app state. But the shipped artifact is a runtime asset, not generated source code, and no component-to-code mapping into the developer's own UI code is documented. Missing for 10: component-to-code mappings to app framework components, generated production source code, independent hands-on corroboration of the design-to-production workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, designs map to production code — component-to-code mappings or direct design-to-code output I can actually ship

citations.quote: What you build in the editor is what ships in your app, game, or website.
You can use the same exported file across supported runtimes, including web, mobile, game engines, and other platforms.
The Rive runtimes are open-source libraries that allow you to load and control your animations in apps, games, and websites.
Loads .riv files, advances state machines and animations, and draws via the abstract Renderer interface.
When data changes, your scene updates automatically.
